description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and accuracy (ACC, y-axis) for six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and an unlabeled gray bar—applied to editing large language models for long-tail biomedical knowledge. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” spans from 0 to approximately 5000 and uses a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 0, 10¹, 10², 10³, and 10⁴. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, ranges from 35% to 65% with linear spacing and tick marks every 5 percentage points. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at ~39% ACC at low co-occurrence and plateaus near 44% as co-occurrence increases. The FT method (blue line with downward-pointing triangular markers) begins at ~40% and rises gradually to ~48%. The IKE method (red line with upward-pointing triangular markers) starts at ~43% and increases to ~49.5%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at ~44%, rises steadily, and reaches ~56.5% at the highest co-occurrence. The MEMIT method (purple line with pentagonal markers) starts at ~44%, increases to ~54.5%, and shows a slight flattening at higher values. The green line with square markers (labeled in legend but without a method name in the legend key, and corresponding to a gray bar in the legend) begins at ~51% and rises sharply to ~66% at the highest co-occurrence, showing the steepest growth among all methods. The gray bar in the legend appears to be a placeholder or error, as no corresponding line is visible in the plot.
